Covered · Session 02M01 / M02

KPIs, variables, grain & data stories

Give every measure a contract

Choose a valid measure, keep denominators visible, and match the display to the variable and question.

Try this session’s experiment →Study mode: notes and interactive lesson →Lab checkpoints →
Study toolkitLaboratoryMind mapInfographicsListenFull slides

Read the session introduction →

What you can explain

  • Identify nominal, ordinal, interval, and ratio measures.
  • Define a KPI's population, unit, denominator, and period.
  • Critique chart scale, aggregation, and the implied story.

Decompose the measure

Construct → operational variable → values

A construct such as satisfaction becomes an observed variable through a stated question or measurement process. Coding does not automatically establish equal intervals.

Connect it to a business example

A single satisfaction item is ordered categorical. Dollar revenue has a meaningful zero and supports ratios.

Choose the right unit

Grain → key → population → period

Keep one observation at the intended grain. Define eligibility and dates before aggregating. A line-item join can duplicate an order-level outcome.

Connect it to a business example

An order with three products is still one order for an order-level late-delivery rate.

Show the denominator

Known outcomes → missing outcomes → bounds

The rate among measured cases answers a different question from the rate among all eligible cases. Unknown outcomes cannot simply be counted as successes.

Connect it to a business example

Show the observed rate and plausible best/worst bounds when outcomes are missing.

Tell a bounded data story

Question → display → interpretation → action

Use bars for category comparisons, histograms for numeric distributions, and scatterplots for two numeric variables. Labels, units, source, and scale support honest comparison.

Connect it to a business example

Start count bars at zero. Joining unordered categories with a line implies an unsupported ordering.
